scope: Read-only catalog codec/replay/journal/generation review, not supervisor integration.

findings.detail: Poison is journal-local, while the supported concurrency test constructs two journal instances in one process. After A writes a complete legal frame and Sync fails, only A is poisoned. B can replay the complete bytes and append another transition. This does not implement the documented supervisor-wide stop after uncertain durability.
findings.reproduction: Open A and B on the same catalog; inject one A.Sync failure after its complete ready frame; restore file Sync; B.Transition(open_recovery_required) currently has no shared poison check and can succeed.
findings.required: Define and enforce supervisor ownership: use a shared poison state for journals of one supervisor, or enforce one journal per supervisor and make multi-supervisor fault tests represent the distinct recovery boundary explicitly. Check poison after acquiring the global lock as necessary to prevent an already-waiting operation from proceeding after another journal poisons the supervisor.
findings.regression: After the first journal's complete-write/Sync failure, a sibling operation in the same supervisor must reject without another write or success; only the explicit new-supervisor startup validation/re-Sync path can authorize recovery.

passed: Both supplied files use the pilot_e2e build tag; no untagged call site was found by the scoped reference search.
CRC-32C framing, repeated length/trailer, canonical re-encoding and contiguous generation validation agree with the reviewed format.
Transition table matches section 109; deleted IDs cannot re-enter provisioning; invalid transitions append no bytes.
Startup replay and file/parent Sync hold the supplied global lock. Journal operations hold local mutex then supplied global lock; this layer never takes a case/bootstrap lock.
Short writes, read/seek failures, Sync failures and unlock errors return fixed errors; no raw I/O error or path is returned.
Concurrent generation test exercises two journal objects with a shared in-process mutex; this is not cross-process OS-lock or full supervisor proof.
test_gaps_before_slice_acceptance: Add valid-CRC malformed JSON records for duplicate/unknown/null/trailing/noncanonical number/key/order cases; current broad corruption tests do not specifically lock these codec contracts.
Add transition-time complete-frame Sync failure and reopen/re-Sync recovery, rather than only bootstrap/startup Sync failures and short writes.
Fault injection for lock/seek/read/stat paths and bounded concurrent completion remain needed for their claimed error contracts.
limitations: No tests or builds were executed.
The test file changed during review to add a platform-lock test; that later addition was not fully reviewed here. Recorded hashes are end-of-read hashes, not a claim of a frozen full-platform review.

OpenVerified handle identity, bootstrap lock ownership, OS cross-process locks, cleanup and supervisor global failure propagation remain integration responsibilities; comments alone do not implement them.
